title: Asking God to Clear My Name
overview: A person who insists they have lived honestly asks God to judge their case, examine their heart, and not let them share the fate of the corrupt.

parts.label: Asking God to judge (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The writer, traditionally David, asks God to declare them in the right, probably against false accusers, though the exact situation is unknown. Their claim of an honest life likely means wholehearted loyalty rather than sinlessness, and they invite God to test their heart the way metal is tested for purity.

parts.label: Keeping away from liars (vv. 4-5)
parts.note: As proof, the writer says they have not joined deceivers, two-faced people or schemers. To sit with someone meant sharing their plans and decisions, not just being in the same room.

parts.label: Clean hands at the altar (vv. 6-8)
parts.note: Washing your hands was a public sign of innocence, and priests washed before approaching the altar where offerings were made. Walking around the altar was probably part of worship at the sanctuary, which the writer loves as the place where God's glory, his felt presence, was believed to live.

parts.label: Do not sweep me away (vv. 9-11)
parts.note: The writer asks not to die alongside violent and corrupt people whose hands are full of bribes, likely meaning those who twist justice for money. Even while claiming integrity, they still ask God for rescue and mercy.

parts.label: Standing on firm ground (v. 12)
parts.note: Level ground pictures a safe, steady footing with nothing to stumble over. The writer ends with confidence, promising to praise God publicly with the gathered community.

disagreement: Christians differ on how to take the writer's claims of innocence: many read them as an honest person's protest against a specific false charge, while others hear them as fully true only in the voice of Jesus, whom Christians see as the one truly innocent person.
think: Is there anyone you would genuinely invite to look closely at your motives, and what would make that feel safe or frightening?
